Long-form piece with h2/h3 hierarchy, a pull quote and an ordered list.
Engineering blog post with inline code, a fenced shell block and a TypeScript block with language classes.
Old-style blog built from divs only (no main/article); sidebar and widgets are classed, not tagged.
Documentation page: breadcrumb, left navigation tree, on-this-page aside, prev/next links around the main content.
API reference with definition lists, a parameters table and an example response.
Rendered repository README: badges, install block, feature list, table of options, licence line.
Issue tracker thread: title, labels, original post and two replies with code.
Encyclopedia-style article: table of contents nav, an infobox table, [edit] section links and a references list.
Forum thread with nested quotes and signatures.
Product page: price, description, specification table, buy button and recommendation widgets.
Recipe page with a long preamble, ingredient list, numbered steps and a large JSON-LD block that must not appear.
Two plain tables with a header row, one with a caption.
A table with colspan and rowspan group headers and right-aligned numbers.
Cells with links, bold, code, a literal pipe, line breaks and an empty cell.
A 1999-style layout table wrapping the content, with a real data table inside.
A 12-column monthly rainfall table with decimals and units in the header.
Three tables interleaved with prose and a list; each must survive separately.
Several code blocks: Python with indentation and blank lines, YAML, a block with tabs and a block without a language.
Syntax-highlighted block where every token is a span and each line a div; text must stay contiguous.
Code containing HTML entities, angle brackets, ampersands and a literal closing tag in a string.
Inline code, kbd and samp inside paragraphs and list items.
Four levels of nested unordered and ordered lists with text after nested lists.
List items containing several paragraphs, a code block and a blockquote.
A glossary built from a definition list with several definitions per term.
Right-to-left Arabic article with dir=rtl, a heading, a list and an embedded Latin term.
Hebrew paragraph mixing numbers, Latin words and punctuation.
Japanese article (UTF-8) with kanji, kana, full-width punctuation and a table.
Simplified Chinese news item with a numbered list.
Korean paragraph with spaces, hanja-free text and a heading.
German article with umlauts, sharp s and typographic quotes.
Shift_JIS bytes with only a <meta charset> declaration (no header charset).
GBK bytes declared only in the Content-Type header.
Windows-1252 bytes (curly quotes, euro sign, e-acute) declared in the header.
The header names a charset the decoder does not know; the <meta> declaration (UTF-8) must be used.
UTF-16LE with a byte-order mark and no charset anywhere else.
UTF-8 with a byte-order mark and a generic text/html type.
Latin-1 bytes with no charset in header, BOM or meta; the sniffing step must not produce replacement characters.
Named, decimal and hex entities, non-breaking spaces, and entity-like text that must stay literal.
Unclosed paragraphs, list items, table cells and a missing </body></html>.
Mis-nested inline tags, stray < and > characters in text, an unterminated attribute quote and a comment that never ends.
A bare fragment: no html, head or body, no doctype.
Unquoted and duplicate attributes, uppercase tags, self-closing syntax on non-void elements.
300 nested divs around two paragraphs; the depth cap must degrade, not lose the text.
Cookie consent overlay (by id, class and role=dialog) in front of full article text.
An article that carries paywall markup (metered, hidden by stylesheet) but includes the full text: must be returned, not refused.
A long article that merely embeds a reCAPTCHA widget in its comment form: must NOT be classified as a CAPTCHA wall.
Head metadata: canonical, published time, language; relative canonical must resolve.
Relative, root-relative, protocol-relative, parent-relative, fragment, mailto and javascript: links resolve (or drop) correctly.
Images with alt text, without alt, decorative (empty alt) and inside links.
Hidden elements (hidden attribute, aria-hidden, display:none) are dropped; visible text is kept.
Server-rendered app: content already inside #root together with a large script bundle; must not be treated as client-rendered.
Client-rendered shell that ships its real content inside <noscript>: with no browser available, that content must be used instead of failing.
text/plain is returned as written.
A Markdown source served as text/markdown is returned untouched, headings included.
A JSON API response is pretty-printed.
An Atom feed is returned as text so the entries can be read.
CSV is returned as written.
A real HTML page served as application/octet-stream (typical object-store misconfiguration) is sniffed and extracted.
A real HTML page served as text/plain is recognised by its doctype and extracted.
No Content-Type header at all; the body is sniffed as HTML.
Content-Encoding: gzip.
Content-Encoding: br.
Content-Encoding: deflate.
Shift_JIS bytes that are additionally gzip-compressed: decompress first, then decode.
Five mixed 301/302/303/307/308 hops end at an article; the final URL is reported.
Redirects with relative and query-bearing Location headers.
A 404 page with a friendly body.
A 410 with a short explanation.
401 with a WWW-Authenticate challenge.
403 whose body is a sign-in form with a password field.
A 200 page that is only a sign-in form (soft login wall).
A 402 Payment Required.
200 with a two-sentence teaser, a visible paywall prompt and JSON-LD marking the article as not free.
429 with Retry-After in seconds.
429 with Retry-After as an HTTP date three minutes in the future.
429 without Retry-After.
A 500 with an HTML error page.
A 503 maintenance page.
The server itself answers 408 Request Timeout.
A gateway answers 504.
A 403 interstitial with a managed-challenge widget (Just a moment...).
A 200 page that is only a reCAPTCHA gate.
A 429 whose body is an hCaptcha challenge: a CAPTCHA, not a plain rate limit.
Content-Length above the cap is refused before the body is read (cap lowered for the test).
A small gzip body that inflates beyond the cap: the cap counts decompressed bytes.
A 500-page manual exceeds a lowered extracted-token cap; the failure is loud, never a truncated success.
A real (generated) text PDF; PDF extraction is not available, so the failure is typed.
A scanned PDF (image only, no text layer); OCR is not available.
A DOCX (zip of XML parts, generated); Office extraction is not available.
An XLSX workbook, same family as DOCX.
A PNG image; no vision route exists in web.fetch.
application/octet-stream whose body is a binary blob.
No Content-Type and a body with NUL bytes.
PDF bytes mislabelled text/html: sniffed by magic number, not turned into garbage Markdown.
ZIP bytes mislabelled text/plain.
Content-Encoding: zstd, which the client does not decode.
An empty root div and a script bundle: client-rendered, no browser available.
A shell with only a loading message and bundles.
A consent wall that holds the whole page back: only consent controls are present, the content is not in the HTML.
Two URLs redirect to each other forever.
Eleven hops with the default limit of ten.
A public-looking page redirects to the cloud metadata address; the hop is refused.
A redirect to ftp:// is refused.
A redirect to file:// is refused.
A redirect target with embedded credentials is refused.
With no allowlist, the loopback address of the fixture server itself is refused before any request.
ftp:// is not fetched.
Not a URL at all.
Credentials in the URL are refused.
An unknown argument name.
maxTokens below the minimum.
A section that does not exist in the page.
A cursor that was never issued.
A cursor from agent A presented by agent B.
robots.txt disallows the path and the call is a crawl.
robots.txt answers 503; a crawl treats that as disallow.
The server accepts the connection and never answers.
Headers arrive, then the body stalls.
The server resets the connection.
Nothing listens on the port.
Content-Encoding: gzip with a corrupt stream.
An https server whose self-signed certificate is not trusted.
Through the tool layer: a document store that throws an unexpected exception is reported as internal-error without leaking the exception text.
A generated 500-page service manual (25 chapters x 20 pages): table of contents, section jumps and a cursor walk must reproduce the whole text with nothing lost.
One 280 000-character line plus a 100 000-character unbroken token: chunking must not lose or split characters.
